terms.latin: īnstrūmentum, īnstrūmentī n. ad pōma dēcorticanda
terms.comment: Our description: a tool for peeling fruit. Traupman and Morgan–Owens have no word for a peeler: Traupman has the verb, cutem resecāre (pp. 72, 358), and Andresian’s rādula (p. 5) is a grater. Dēcorticāre is classical, of stripping bark (Plin., in Lewis & Short).

sources: Lewis & Short: instrumentum · Lewis & Short: decortico
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, pp. 72, 358.
